=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18525-18540 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When the `/answer` comment POST fails, the code always moves the label back to `ai:awaiting-approval`, even if GitHub accepted the comment and only the response was lost, because `gh_retry` makes just one attempt for a non-idempotent POST (scripts/gh_helpers.sh lines 1206-1213, `_gh_cmd_is_unsafe_post`).
  WHY: An accepted marker can trigger plan.yml, and the rollback can remove `ai:planning` before plan.yml's label check (.github/workflows/plan.yml lines 932-952), so the plan run is skipped; the marker then blocks any further automatic re-plan, the issue's one re-plan is lost, and the issue goes back to a maintainer hold. Reviewers disagree on severity: minimax_minimax-m3 and openai_gpt-6-luna rate it MAJOR, anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rate it NIT (it fails safe to the human hold), and google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite gives no severity. The highest is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18536-18544 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The label rollback (`gh_retry gh issue edit ... --add-label 'ai:awaiting-approval' --remove-label 'ai:planning'`) is a single non-atomic call that can also fail.
  WHY: If both the comment POST and the rollback fail, the issue is left in `ai:planning` with no marker, or with a marker whose response was lost; this is a degraded state that may need manual cleanup and that maintainers cannot tell apart from the logs alone.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18503-18510 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When `phase_cap_can_dispatch "ai:planning" "automation_path_replan"` denies the re-plan, the branch logs only `STALL_SKIP ... reason=phase_capped` and returns 1; it skips both the `AI_PHASE_GATE_V1 ... outcome=defer` line and `_plan_auto_approval_hold_notify`. `phase_cap_can_dispatch` also returns 1 when `PHASE_CAPS_STATUS=actions_runs_unavailable` (lines 17051-17054).
  WHY: If the cap stays full or the snapshot stays unavailable, an eligible hold sits in `ai:awaiting-approval` with no hold notice and no defer line, for an unbounded time, which is worse than the pre-PR behaviour. This only applies when caps are enabled (opt-in). anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 separately ruled that the unavailable-status case cannot reach this branch, because the earlier `ai:implementing` cap checks at lines 18636-18640 and 23269-23271 return first.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:N/A (missing test for scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18503-18510) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: No test covers the new `ai:planning` phase-capped re-plan branch. Every `_replan_run` and `_pipeline_plan_grant_run` case runs with `PHASE_CAPS_ENABLED` unset, so `phase_cap_can_dispatch` returns 0 straight away.
  WHY: A later edit that posts the marker or the hold notice before returning on this branch would silently use up the issue's one automatic re-plan, and CI would not catch it. The cap harness in tests/test_orchestrator_concurrency_caps.py could be reused.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "No action on #8339 itself; its owner unblocks it by hand."
  expected_change_site: eligibility condition in `_plan_auto_approval_gate` in scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh (around lines 18487-18517); google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite also names `_plan_hold_replannable` in scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: `_plan_hold_replannable` and `_plan_auto_approval_gate` check only `path_not_granted`, `replannable`, phase and marker status, with no exclusion for issue #8339. Since #8339's plan has the targeted shape, the first eligible tick after merge would move its label and post the `/answer` re-plan comment. All three flagging reviewers rate it MAJOR. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly rejected this gap: the line is a Non-goal against a one-off fix, and a hard-coded issue-number exclusion would be an invented requirement.
- requirement: "Poller: … an eligible hold with no marker posts one `/answer` comment carrying the marker and no hold notice; …"
  expected_change_site: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The `phase_cap_can_dispatch "ai:planning" "automation_path_replan"` branch at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18503-18510 has no test. A grep for `automation_path_replan` or `phase_capped` in tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py returns zero matches, and every `_replan_run` / `_pipeline_plan_grant_run` test runs with `PHASE_CAPS_ENABLED` unset.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 18525-18540, in the comment-POST failure branch added by the last run: `gh_retry gh issue edit "${issue_num}" ... --add-label 'ai:awaiting-approval' --remove-label 'ai:planning'` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `gh_retry` makes one attempt for a non-idempotent POST (scripts/gh_helpers.sh lines 1206-1213), so a failure does not prove GitHub rejected the comment, yet the rollback treats every failure as "not posted".
  WHY: If the POST was accepted and the rollback lands before plan.yml's label check (.github/workflows/plan.yml lines 932-952), plan.yml skips with `reason=missing_expected_phase_label` and the one re-plan is spent with no plan run. It fails safe to the human hold, and the trigger is narrow. Suggested mitigation: re-read the comments once on this branch and skip the rollback if the marker is present.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:the new #8339 tests (`_replan_run`, `test_managed_replannable_hold_*`, `test_standalone_replannable_hold_posts_one_replan_answer`); untested branch scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 18503-18510 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `ai:planning` cap wait has no test; nothing asserts that a capped run makes no label edit and posts no `/answer`, marker or hold notice.
  WHY: A later edit that posts the marker or hold notice before returning would silently use up the one re-plan; the harness in tests/test_orchestrator_concurrency_caps.py could be reused.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
